question: A 37-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing swelling and pain of his right knee for the past month. He has not had any trauma to the knee or previous problems with his joints. He has hypertension. His only medication is hydrochlorothiazide. He works as a carpet installer. He drinks two to three beers daily. He is 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 97 kg (214 lb); BMI is 33.6 kg/m2. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 122/82 mm Hg. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema; there is fluctuant edema over the lower part of the patella. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. The skin over the site of his pain is not warm. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella; there is no joint line tenderness. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Swelling and pain in right knee" -> "No history of trauma or joint problems" -> "Hypertension and hydrochlorothiazide use" -> "Occupation as a carpet installer" -> "Alcohol consumption" -> "Obesity (BMI 33.6)" -> "Limited flexion due to pain" -> "Fluctuant edema over lower part of patella" -> "Tenderness on palpation of patella" -> "No joint line tenderness" -> "Not warm skin over the site of pain" -> "Most likely diagnosis is prepatellar bursitis" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 37-year-old man with swelling and pain in his right knee, hypertension, hydrochlorothiazide use, occupation as a carpet installer, alcohol consumption, and obesity (BMI 33.6) is prepatellar bursitis. This is supported by the presence of fluctuant edema over the lower part of the patella, tenderness on palpation of the patella, limited flexion due to pain, and absence of joint line tenderness or warm skin over the site of pain.
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for the 37-year-old man with swelling and pain in his right knee, hypertension, hydrochlorothiazide use, occupation as a carpet installer, alcohol consumption, and obesity (BMI 33.6) is prepatellar bursitis. This is supported by the presence of fluctuant edema over the lower part of the patella, tenderness on palpation of the patella, limited flexion due to pain, and absence of joint line tenderness or warm skin over the site of pain. Gout typically presents with acute onset, septic arthritis would likely have more systemic symptoms, osteoarthritis is less likely in a younger individual without a history of joint problems, and Osgood-Schlatter disease is typically seen in adolescents and presents with pain and swelling below the knee.
